mechanism.base: Fire feeds Earth, the old texts say. What burns comes down as ash, and ash is the first soil. Every field that grows was warmed before it was planted. The flame readies the ground rather than building it, loosening the cold and leaving a fine black dust that holds water and seed. The ground remembers each fire as a richer season, and a long cold year as a thin harvest.
mechanism.catalyst_turn: With too little Fire, the ground goes cold under the seed, and the soil feeds on an old harvest. Take in one warm thing a week, a teacher or a book.
mechanism.friction_turn: With too much Fire, the soil bakes to a hard dry crust over the seed, and nothing planted in it comes up. Make one thing from all you took in and hand it over.

function.definition_catalyst: Your Mind is where the world soaks in and becomes yours. Fire makes it warm, and you keep what lights you up. As a catalyst, your Mind is left wanting, so you either chase hunches alone or wait to be taught. You end up circling the same few ideas.
function.definition_friction: Your Mind is where the world soaks in and becomes yours. What moves you stays, because Fire keeps it warm. As a friction, you keep taking in after you have enough, sheltering an idea or a person rather than testing either. You know far more than you ever tried.
function.advise_catalyst: You learn by being warmed, and warmth is something you have to go and sit near. Once a month sit in on a class or a talk as a listener only. Keep one person you can ask the simple question, and ask it. Read one slow chapter before sleep each night.
function.advise_friction: Seek Water, the Action energy. Water runs down, cools what it touches and carries it away. Let it spend what Fire burns. You have taken in more than you will ever use, and each new idea costs you the last. Decide one open question by a date. Fix one small thing at home with what you already know.

candidates.cta_verdict: You take a thing in once you see why it matters to you, so you tend to ask what it is for more than how it works.

catalyst.clause: The ground goes cold under the seed.
catalyst.remedy: Take in one warm thing a week, a teacher or a book.

friction.clause: The soil bakes to a hard dry crust over the seed.
friction.remedy: Make one thing from all you took in and hand it over.

wide.clause: You were given plenty of Fire, the warmth every harvest starts from.
wide.remedy: Use it. Start what you keep studying.

missing.clause: Without fire there is no ash, and this ground has nothing new to grow from.
missing.remedy: Stay close to people who love what they learn.

spared.clause: No fire reaches this soil, and it keeps its water the better for it.
spared.remedy: Leave it unlit and build with what you have.

thin.clause: A small fire warms this ground without drying it, the right size for the soil.
thin.remedy: Keep it small, one lamp at a time.

excess.clause: Fire past its use scorches the very ground it was lit to feed.
excess.remedy: Stop adding. Let the ground cool before you learn more.

catalyst.clause: The field goes gray: duties held on cold ground, nothing warm coming in.

mechanism_yin.base: Ash is earth, the old texts say: everything that burns comes down to soil at last. So the field is fed by every fire that visits it, warmth breaking down into richness, the bright and the festive settling in as fertility. Cold ground grows little. Ground that has known flame grows the harvest.
mechanism_yin.catalyst_turn: Run thin, the field goes gray: duties held on cold ground, nothing warm coming in. Your chart asks you to feed the fire that feeds you. Accept warmth. Attend the feast.

__ore.retired_fn_body: The Root is your learning function: the seat where the world soaks in and becomes yours. With Fire running it, your mind absorbs through warmth: stories told at tables, lessons carried by people you love, knowledge that arrives lit. You learn best in company and remember what was taught with feeling. Seek warm teachers. Cold material simply never composts into you.
__ore.retired_base_personal: Your core is Earth, and Fire feeds Earth: ash becomes soil. Everything warm that visits you, affection, praise, festivity, sunlight on the field, breaks down into the ground you grow from. That is why Fire is your Mind, the intake that restores what holding spends. Soil is not made by stone alone. It is made by everything that once burned.

backlog_dips_tg_pattern.body: Celebration is restoration: sun, feasts, and open affection literally rebuild your ground.

__ore.retired_v3_definition_catalyst:
Fire is your Mind, and as a catalyst, it is how learning actually enters you: through excitement, people, and live example rather than cold text. You retain what warmed you. Affection, praise, and festivity all count as study.

The lecture you remember came from the teacher you loved. The skill that stuck was learned beside someone, the fact that stayed arrived inside a story, and everything studied dutifully alone has mostly evaporated.

For you, warmth is a study technique. Take the class instead of the book. Explain new ideas to someone within a day of meeting them. Learn beside people on purpose, and let excitement pick the syllabus more often than duty does.
__ore.retired_v3_definition_friction:
Fire is your Mind, and as a friction, it is stimulation mistaken for nourishment: feeds, sparks, novelty consumed all day while real understanding stays shallow. The excitement is spending you, and it feels like input.

Interested in everything for about a minute. Forty tabs of sparks, a feed refreshed at red lights, enthusiasm rented by the hour, and by evening the mind is somehow both overfull and unfed.

Attention is the meal, and yours is being eaten as snacks. Cut the feeds to one sitting a day. Give the freed hour to one slow subject and stay a month. Let yourself be bored on purpose until depth becomes interesting again.
